claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my one child, Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's lovely to meet you. Let me ask a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask about your own circumstances.

Are you responsible for Alex? This would typically mean you pay for things like their food, clothes, and accommodation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex - I pay for all their food, clothes, and everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

Could you tell me a bit about your immigration or residency status? Specifically:

1. Do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, are you a British citizen, have settled status, or have another form of leave to remain)?
2. Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions:

Is Alex in full-time education, or are they currently working or in training? And if they are in education, is this at a school or college (not university)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is still at school - just doing their GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Just one final question:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules, I now have everything I need to make a determination about your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

Let me summarise what you've told me:
- Alex is 15 years old
- Alex lives with you
- You are responsible for Alex (paying for food, clothes, etc.)
- You live in the UK and have the right to live here
- Alex is in full-time education (doing GCSEs at school)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **Age**: Alex is 15, which is under 16
- ✅ **Residence**: You live in the UK and have the right to live here
- ✅ **Responsibility**: Alex lives with you and you're responsible for their care
- ✅ **Education**: Alex is in full-time education at school
- ✅ **No duplicate claims**: No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You can apply for Child Benefit online through the GOV.UK website. It's also worth noting that even if your income is over £60,000, it can still be worth claiming Child Benefit as it helps you build up National Insurance credits and your child will automatically get a National Insurance number when they turn 16.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
